elements.problem: Encoded as any Hemoptysis; the volume threshold is lost, so any blood-streaked sputum triggers Urgent (over-triage). Volume is not representable in the language, so this is a known approximation.
evidence: Urgent: suspected TB with danger signs :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Hemoptysis" "finding"))

elements.problem: TB symptoms cough, weight loss, night sweats, fever encoded as possible TB. Cough and fever are anchored; 'current' and 'drenching' not expressed. Weight decreased/cough are broad.

elements.scope_reason: Mostly management; contains diagnostic logic 'HIV and TB symptoms and CD4 <= 200 or WHO stage 3/4 -> urine LAM; LAM positive -> diagnose TB'. CD4 has no unit in the language; LAM result is a lab test.
parts_missing: Diagnose TB on positive urine LAM
elements.problem: No probable/confirmed TB diagnosis rule for LAM positive.
MTB detected NAAT positive is a lab result branch; no confirmed-TB rule. Flowchart branches (treated in last 2 years, DST) not encoded.

elements.scope_reason: 'Diagnose INH-resistant TB' is a diagnosis conclusion but depends on DST lab result (not representable).
'Diagnose RR-TB' is a diagnosis conclusion but depends on DST lab result (not representable).

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for urgent suspected TB conditions (task) / system_diagnosis_rule
rule_level_problems.problem: Possible-TB rule omits two of the page's 'test even without symptoms' triggers (recent DS-TB treatment, PLHIV/pregnant at first antenatal visit); only symptoms, contact and CXR are encoded.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: suspected TB with danger signs
rule_level_problems.problem: Hemoptysis fires without the >= 1 tablespoon volume; Drowsy/confused narrowed to Acute confusion.
No TB diagnosis rule for confirmed pathways (NAAT positive, urine LAM, INH-resistant, RR-TB); these depend on lab results and are arguably not representable.

Broad evidence: any Cough, Weight decreased or Fever makes TB possible, which then combines with any danger sign (e.g. Fever > 39 alone) to give Urgent. Page logic is 'suspected TB' so acceptable but over-triages.

summary: Red-box danger signs are well encoded (13 criteria, all with plausible concepts and correct thresholds), with minor fidelity losses on haemoptysis volume, 'confused' narrowing and malnutrition concept. The most consequential gap is that the possible-TB rule misses the page's 'test even without symptoms' triggers (recent TB treatment, PLHIV, pregnancy) and no diagnostic conclusions (LAM, INH-resistant, RR-TB) exist, though these are largely lab-dependent.
